tells: Chassis (olive/grey) reads as one flat untextured material: uniform value across stock, receiver area and forend, only a faint fine noise; no anodize/Cerakote sheen variation, no edge wear, no handling polish on the forend or grip
Edges on the chassis are near-sharp CG creases (forend top rail, lightening-slot rims, stock comb block) with no consistent machined chamfer catching a highlight line
Stock/cheek-riser block top-left is a plain box with a single slot; no adjustment wheel, buttons or lock hardware detail; looks like blockout

Scope tube, turrets and rings are uniform matte dark grey with soft plastic-like shading; turret caps have no engraved numbers/hash marks, power ring has no raised index or grip ribs that read as real
Objective lens is a flat purple-blue disc with no internal lens-element reflections, no coating colour shift, no reflection of the environment
Bolt body is dull grey instead of bright jewelled/polished steel; bolt handle knob is a plain sphere with a straight thin rod that looks too skinny and uniform
Magazine is a flat box with vertical grooves, same matte value as plastic; no metal/polymer distinction, no witness holes or follower visible
Pistol grip has a noise texture painted over hard faceted geometry; faceting reads as low-poly with no finger-groove softness
Trigger is a flat curved plate with no thickness variation; trigger guard is the chassis colour with no separation
Lighting: flat studio grey void with soft global light and no contact shadow or ground; no specular hotspots anywhere on the metal
Same flat single-tone chassis material; stock buttplate block is a stack of grey boxes with no rubber pad texture or spacers
Two round flush discs on the stock side look like placeholder buttons, not real hardware
Bipod legs are uniform black cylinders, very thin and straight; extension sections have shiny chrome bands that look pasted; feet are simple black cylinders with no rubber texture or flex
Bipod sits floating with no ground plane or shadow; legs canted inward symmetrically like a rig pose, not resting under load
Fluted barrel has clean flutes but zero muzzle detail at this angle and no blueing/finish variation; reads as procedural
Bolt body shows a mirror-chrome stripe that is the only shiny part of the gun; contrast with everything else looks CG
Scope rail on top of the receiver/mount has teeth but no recoil-lug slot spacing logic, uniform blocks
At 35 cm the lack of surface detail is glaring: chassis is a smooth olive slab with low-frequency noise only, no machining marks, no Cerakote orange peel, no worn edges at the bolt-handle cutout
Bolt body is an over-bright chrome cylinder with a hard white strip highlight; real bolts show turned/jewelled finish and oil/carbon, not a pure mirror
Bolt shroud is a plain cylinder with one small dot; no cocking indicator, firing-pin detail or fine fit lines
Scope eyepiece rim and tube are smooth grey with soft gradient shading and visible faceting on the eyepiece bell silhouette; no rubber eyepiece texture, no diopter markings
Turret and parallax knobs: flat ribbed cylinders, no numbers, no zero-stop marks, no knurl crispness
Ring screws and rail are simple cylinders/boxes; no Torx/hex recesses visible, screws sit on surface like stickers
Bolt knob knurling is a texture on a perfect sphere; at this distance it looks like a golf ball, too regular and too dark matte
Safety lever left of the shroud is a tiny box with a few ribs; selector markings are faint and blurry
Panel joins between chassis pieces show no gap or shadow line; parts intersect instead of meeting
At distance the silhouette is believable, but the rifle floats in an empty grey void with no shadow or contact
Chassis is flat pale grey-green with almost no shading gradient; reads like a matte clay render
Objective lens shows a saturated purple disc that pops as CG
Stock block is overly boxy and pale, value too close to the background, killing depth
Bipod legs read as thin black sticks with chrome dots
No reticle, no exit pupil, no sight picture at all: the eyepiece is an opaque near-black disc
Inside the eyepiece you can see a faint box-like room/reflection with straight vertical seams, which looks like a CG environment, not optics
Eyepiece rim silhouette is visibly polygonal on the left and right edges with a hard white rim-light line
No eyebox shading (black ring / scope shadow) that a real eye position produces; no lens glass reflection or coating tint

priorities: Give the chassis a real finish material: Cerakote/anodize with roughness breakup (orange-peel micro normal, roughness variation 0.45-0.7), subtle colour variation, edge wear to bare metal on high points (bolt cutout, forend edges, stock corners), and handling polish/grime in grip and forend areas

Add consistent machined chamfers/fillets (0.5-1.5 mm) on every chassis and receiver edge so each edge catches a thin highlight; add visible panel gaps and shadow lines where chassis parts, mag well and trigger guard meet instead of intersecting

Build a working ADS view: reticle (mil-dot/tree) on a lens plane, exit-pupil scope shadow vignette, render-target or magnified view through the objective; remove the visible box reflection and increase eyepiece segment count
Fix glass: objective and ocular lenses need multi-layer coating tint (green/amber/purple shift by angle), environment reflection, and visible internal lens elements instead of a flat purple disc

Rework the bolt: turned/jewelled steel with anisotropic highlight, light oil/carbon near the lugs, not a pure chrome stripe; add bolt-shroud detail (cocking indicator, firing pin), thicken and taper the bolt handle, and give the knob a tactical oval or crisper knurl rather than a perfect sphere

Add scope markings and knurling: turret numerals and hash marks, zero-stop lines, magnification ring numbers with raised index, ribbed rubber eyepiece, parallax numbers; generic brand-free laser engraving on tube
Detail the stock/butt assembly: rubber recoil pad with texture, LOP spacers, cheek-riser adjustment knob and lock lever, sling QD cups; replace the two flat discs with real hardware
Bipod: thicken legs, add proper extension notches/latch buttons, rubber feet with texture, anodized finish with wear; pose it under load with a ground plane

Differentiate materials: polymer mag and grip (softer roughness, mold texture) vs steel barrel (parkerized/nitride, slight blueing variation, muzzle device detail) vs aluminium rings and rail; add Torx/hex recesses to every screw
Render on a ground plane or HDRI with contact shadows and stronger key/rim lighting so specular response is visible; current flat grey void lighting itself reads CG
